question.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]x(t)+\overset{f(t)}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ 5{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]}},\,Φ=[\begin{aligned}0 & {e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{2t} & -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations and the fundamental matrix of the corresponding homogeneous system above. Using the method of variation of parameters, compute ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)$ and the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t)$ of the system.
${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,,\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)={e}^{t}\,\,$ {{field-2}}
$2{e}^{2t}$ $-8$
question.worked_solution:
We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}0 & {e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{2t} & -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ 5{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{0\cdot (-{e}^{-t})-{e}^{-t}\cdot {e}^{2t}}[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ -{e}^{2t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =-{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ -{e}^{2t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ 5{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7{e}^{-t} \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}7{e}^{-t} \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 7{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int 2{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7{e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & {e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{2t} & -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-7{e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ -8{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
